subject.title: fix: mobile pairing should advertise usable LAN and Tailnet routes

question: Should mobile setup codes add a backward-compatible advertised route list, and what route ordering plus security rules should govern LAN, Tailnet Serve, direct tailnet, and manual public URLs?
rationale: The fix crosses gateway protocol, bootstrap-token setup payloads, and mobile client fallback behavior, so automation should not choose the permanent route contract or security policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add validated route list
options.body: Keep the legacy `url`, add a route-list field, prefer secure Tailnet/remote routes when present, allow cleartext only for currently allowed LAN/local routes, and update both mobile clients to fall back through the list.

options.title: Prefer a single secure remote URL
options.body: Avoid a route-list contract for now and make setup-code generation prefer configured Tailscale/remote URLs over LAN when they are discoverable.

options.title: Defer to broader remote pairing work
options.body: Leave this issue open until the broader mobile/Tailscale pairing direction in related issues is settled, accepting that this specific setup path remains blocked meanwhile.

recommendation.title: Add validated route list
recommendation.body: Keep the legacy `url`, add a route-list field, prefer secure Tailnet/remote routes when present, allow cleartext only for currently allowed LAN/local routes, and update both mobile clients to fall back through the list.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is assigned on the live issue and current-main history points to recent ownership of the setup-code/mobile pairing surface.
